Make Solar Customer Reports Traceable to Evidence

Thematic Area: Solar Performance Reporting & Customer Proof

How might we prepare clear solar customer reports whose performance figures and claims can be traced to approved supporting records?

Background

An Indonesian solar EPC business publishes project information and offers maintenance reporting. The opportunity is to connect customer performance reports with traceable supporting records.

The objective is to prepare clear reports covering generation, maintenance actions and documented savings assumptions. Relevant startups offer document review, evidence tracing and numerical consistency checks.

The solution should connect report figures with the relevant reporting periods, calculations and operating records, while supporting technical approval and customer permission for external use.

Significance of Problem

Without an effective solution, the challenges include:

  • Harder performance review: Customers need clear evidence and assumptions to assess reported performance.
  • More review effort: Inconsistent figures across drafts and supporting records increase checking and correction work.
  • Limited reuse of results: Complete evidence and approvals help teams use reports in renewals, references and customer communications.

Existing Efforts

  • Opportunity focus: Create a consistent link between customer-report claims, supporting records and reviewer approval.
  • Available partner capabilities: An AI document-review provider traces findings to supporting passages and supports reviewer comments and sign-off. A university numerical-document research method offers a basis for developing comparisons between reported quantities and supporting records.
  • Collaboration focus: Select a customer report, organise supporting records and trace its figures and claims through review. Technical staff approve calculations, periods and assumptions, with customer approval for external use. Develop and test numerical checking as part of the review workflow.

Potential Market Size

  • Expanding solar reporting base: Global installed PV capacity reached 2.96 TW at end-2025, providing a growing asset base for customer performance reporting.

Eligibility / Qualification

  • Technology readiness: Minimum technology readiness level 3 (TRL3).
  • NUS linkage: NUS student or graduate founder, or incubation through an NUS programme such as BLOCK71.
  • Local and overseas startups: Open to Indonesian and overseas startups.
  • Commitment: Complete the selection process and travel to Indonesia if selected.
